archetype.name: Title Contender (size-and-glass two-way)
archetype.definition: A top-four team by Net Rtg whose 11-3 record matches its scoring margin exactly. It is built on an elite half-court offense fed by second chances, with a defense that sits in the league's top third.

report.headline: Houston's 11-3 is earned by margin, with an offense that finally caught up
report.take:
Houston has spent four seasons climbing: 20-62, then 22-60, 41-41 and two straight 52-30 years. The constant through the rise was defense, with Def Rank 9, 4 and 6. The offense lagged at 20th, 13th and 8th. This year the offense jumped to 2nd, with an ORtg of 122.3 against a league average of 114.2. That makes the Rockets a different kind of team, not just a better version of last year's.

The offense is not built on volume threes. Houston's 3PA Rate of 39.3 ranks 23rd and sits below the league average. It wins on shot quality and extra shots instead. The eFG % of 55.9 is 3rd and the 3P % of 37.8 is 6th. The ORB % of 32.4 is 2nd, and that is no fluke: it was 34.8 last year and 31.7 the year before. Şengün is the engine, with a BPM of 9.2 and a 3rd-place rank on the center tab. Durant (6th among small forwards) and Jabari Smith Jr. (5th among power forwards) give the wings and frontcourt their A+ grades.

The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0, the margin implies 11 wins, and the differential per game of 10.14 ranks 4th. The part to doubt is the defense. Opponents are shooting 32.5% from three, 2nd-best in the league and well below last year's 35.1. Behind that, the rim protection is mediocre (Opp Rim FG % 66.6, 20th) and the defensive glass has slipped to a DRB % of 72.3 (19th), below every recent Houston season. Some of the defensive rating is three-point luck. When it fades, this looks more like a Def Rank 12-15 group than a top-10 one.

The backcourt is the soft spot. It grades C+, VanVleet is out, and Smart is listed with a suspension. VanVleet's +8.2 On-Off and 3.6 BPM led the guards, and Sheppard has been inefficient at a 50.1 TS % on a 21.2 USG %. That shifts more creation onto Şengün and Durant. The big-man depth is also thinner than it looks, with Capela out. Houston is still a 55-plus-win team on this evidence, but it is a contender whose margin for injury is narrower than the 11-3 suggests.

strengths.title: Efficient half-court offense, not variance
strengths.body: An ORtg of 122.3 ranks 2nd. It comes from shot quality (eFG % 3rd) rather than three-point volume, where Houston ranks 23rd in 3PA Rate. Its scoring therefore depends less on hot shooting nights than a high-volume team's would. Some cooling from 37.8% is likely, but the shot profile holds up.

strengths.title: Offensive glass is a trademark
strengths.body: The ORB % of 32.4 ranks 2nd and follows a 34.8 mark last season, so it is identity rather than a hot start. Second chances turn decent possessions into points and give the offense a floor when shots stop falling.

strengths.title: Şengün plus elite forwards
strengths.body: Şengün's BPM of 9.2 and team-best Win Shares make him the hub. Durant scores efficiently at a 63.8 TS %, and Smith's +19 On-Off is the team's best. Three top-six players at their positions give Houston a high floor in any given week.

concerns.title: Defense propped up by opponent shooting
concerns.body: Opp 3P % of 32.5 ranks 2nd, yet the rim defense ranks 20th and the defensive rebounding 19th. Opponent three-point shooting is the least stable number in a 14-game sample. Expect the DRtg of 111.8 to drift toward last year's level as it normalizes.

concerns.title: Guard depth is thin right now
concerns.body: The backcourt grades C+ even with VanVleet. With him out and Smart suspended, Sheppard's 50.1 TS % becomes a bigger share of the guard minutes. This is fixable when the absences end, but it is the one roster group that can't absorb losses.

concerns.title: Scoring dipped in November
concerns.body: Points per game fell from 120.71 in October to 116 in November while points allowed held steady. The decline is mild, but it lines up with the guard absences and bears watching if they last.

trend.note: October went 6-1 and November 5-2. The last 10 games carried a 10.3 margin per game, essentially the season rate, so the team has stayed at the same level without real swings. The one wobble was a three-loss stretch in early November, followed by five straight wins.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, but only Denver looks like a real test
weekAhead.body:
Houston opens at Miami, Indiana and Denver before hosting the Clippers. Miami and Indiana rank 16th and 22nd on the site, and the Clippers are 4-8. Miami's defense ranks 22nd, with an Opp eFG % of 57 (28th), and it plays fast at a pace of 102. That clashes with Houston's 96.8, so controlling tempo matters there. Indiana is the worst offensive-rebounding team in the league, which suits Houston's strongest habit.

Denver is the swing game. Houston already beat the Nuggets 110-100 at home, but this one is in Denver. The Nuggets have allowed the fewest points to opposing centers, so Şengün may have to work harder there. The Clippers shoot 39.1% from three and could test whether Houston's opponent three-point shooting is real. They also turn it over at a 15.7 TOV %, among the worst rates in the league. A 3-1 week is the baseline.

keyMatchups.title: Durant and Thompson vs. Indiana wings
keyMatchups.body: Indiana allows 28.14 points a game to small forwards, 29th in the league, and its wings grade D-. Houston's A+ wing group should find easy offense there.

keyMatchups.title: Smith Jr. vs. Denver at PF
keyMatchups.body: Denver gives up 27.82 points a game to power forwards (29th) and the most threes to the position. Their centers, though, allow the fewest points. Expect Houston's offense in Denver to tilt toward Smith rather than Şengün.

keyMatchups.title: Miami's leaky guard defense
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows 31.92 points a game to point guards and 31.77 to shooting guards, both near the bottom of the league. Houston's guard rotation is depleted, though, so it is unclear who cashes in. Sheppard and Bogdanović get the chance to.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Houston's opponents keep missing threes, especially the Clippers' 39.1% shooters on Sunday.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation holds. The margin is real (W vs Pt Diff of 0), the offensive rebounding is a multi-year trait, and the top three players rank among the best at their positions. The 64-win pace will not survive 68 more games, though. Opponent three-point shooting should regress, and the defense looks closer to league-average quality at the rim than the rating shows. A realistic finish is in the mid-to-high 50s with a Net Rtg in the 7 to 9 range, which still beats last year's 5.4.

The division race with San Antonio at 12-2 will likely go deep into the season, so seeding depends on the backcourt getting healthy. Houston's ceiling depends on the guards producing enough that Şengün and Durant aren't asked to carry every possession.

confidence.note: 14 games; the margin and history back it, but the shooting splits are small samples.
